# Full source parity does not give Gamma whole-fiber response weight, even for the best menu

There is an actual n=1,d=2 four-fiber family with exactly two deepest
sources, occupying both parities, and with zero outside coarea for EVERY
active cap at either source. The midpoint forest assigns the left endpoint
fiber to source0. Nevertheless EVERY balanced active menu at source0
captures that whole fiber with response weight less than3/8<Gamma_2=4/9.

This is a best-menu obstruction, not a poorly chosen prescribed menu.
It does not obstruct convex-field capacity: one complete own triangle
facet is isolatable and pays strictly more than Gamma_2 for sufficiently
small positive smoothing width. All assertions below concern actual
all-normal cap minima and actual deepest marks. The body is not asserted
to minimize the global body variational problem.

## 1. The complete compatible family

Use continuous coordinates (x,y) and put

    T={x>=-1, y>=-1, x+y<=1}, V=|T|=9/2,
    A=(-1,-1), B=(2,-1), C=(-1,2).

Fix a sufficiently small sigma>0, with sigma<=10^(-4), and set

    D=(1-sigma)A+sigma T, v=|D|=V sigma^2,
    b=1-4sigma, r=-8sigma,
    R=[-1,b]^2,
    E_L=[r-L,r]^2,      2sqrt(sigma)<=L<=4sqrt(sigma).

At integer bases -1,0,1,2 prescribe D,T,R,E_L respectively. They are
the exact sampled fibers of their canonical convex hull. Indeed

    (D+R)/2 subset T, (T+E_L)/2 subset R.             (1)

For the first inclusion both coordinates are at least-1, while the
maximum sum is

    [(-2+3sigma)+2b]/2=-5sigma/2<1.

For the second, each coordinate belongs to

    [(-1+r-L)/2,(2+r)/2] subset [-1,b],

since r-L>=-1 and (2+r)/2=b. These two adjacent midpoint inclusions
make every continuous support-height sequence concave on the four
equally spaced bases. Its piecewise-affine concave interpolation
therefore majorizes every barycentric support combination at an integer
base. Thus taking the full canonical hull introduces no extra fiber
points, not merely no extra midpoint points. P={-1,0,1,2} is complete.

Let Sigma(sigma,L) be the actual positive pooled within-fiber covariance.
It is invariant under exchanging x and y. Use the pure outward uniform
kernel with width h Gamma(u), Gamma(u)=sqrt(u^T Sigma u). Sigma is computed
from these actual fibers; no independent covariance is chosen.

## 2. The exact zero-width triangle source

Write a diagonal triangle mark in barycentric coordinates as

    (y_A,y_B,y_C)=(1-2t,t,t),
    (x,y)=(3t-1,3t-1).

The minimum ordinary cap area in the branch whose maximum vertex is A,
B, or C is, near the centroid,

    q_A=4V t^2, q_B=q_C=4V t(1-2t).                 (2)

Each minimizing branch direction is unique and its proper section has
centroid at the mark. For completeness, when a cap isolates vertex i,
its two edge-intercept ratios l_j,l_k satisfy
y_j/l_j+y_k/l_k=1; AM-GM gives l_j l_k>=4y_j y_k,
with equality only at l_j=2y_j,l_k=2y_k. At the centroid, two-vertex
caps have area at least V/2>4V/9. Compactness then keeps branch minima
away from those combinatorial boundaries for marks near the centroid.
The strict AM-GM minimum has positive angular second derivative.

The A branch will capture D, and the B,C branches will miss all outside
fibers. Equating their total masses gives

    12t^2-4t+sigma^2=0,
    t=t_sigma=(1+sqrt(1-3sigma^2))/6,
    Q_0=q_A+v=q_B=q_C.                              (3)

Here 1/4<t<1/3 and

    2<=Q_0<=2+v.                                    (4)

The three normals form a strictly positive circuit and span R^2.

## 3. Global outside quotas at source0, for EVERY normal and base tilt

Write an arbitrary cap through Y=(0,s,s), with s near 3t_sigma-1, as

    a z+u.(X-(s,s))>=0,

with the actual outward smoothing of width h Gamma(u).

If A is a maximum vertex of u on T, then u_x<=0,u_y<=0. Its outside
capture is at least v for EVERY real a. In fact, if D is not fully
captured, some X_D in D has

    -a+u.(X_D-Y)<0, hence a>u.(X_D-Y).

For every X in the fixed square [-1/2,1/2]^2 subset R, both coordinates
of X_D+X-2Y are negative, for sigma and |s| sufficiently small. Thus

    a+u.(X-Y)>u.(X_D+X-2Y)>0.

The entire area-one square is captured from R, which exceeds v. Hence

    outside mass>=v;
    equality forces D fully captured and R,E_L completely missed. (5)

This argument is unaffected by outward smoothing: positive margin means
kernel value1, while failure of full capture supplies a negative margin.

For either the B or C branch, outside mass is of course nonnegative.
The relevant own branch minima attain outside mass zero. To see the
strict margins, at h=0 normalize the B direction with first coordinate1:

    u_B=(1,delta), u_C=(delta,1),
    delta=3-1/t_sigma=O(sigma^2)<0.

Choose a_B=a_C=-1+(7/2)sigma. At sigma=0 the two restrictive margins
on D and R are zero; the displayed perturbation makes both at most
-sigma/2+O(sigma^2). On E_L they are bounded above by -1 for small
sigma. These remain below the whole outward strip for small h.
For A, u_A=(-1,-1) and a_A=-3 strictly capture D and miss R,E_L.

Thus all three desired outside patterns are realized with strict slack.
No assertion about a fixed arbitrary witness menu is being made: (5)
and nonnegativity are bounds for ALL a and ALL u in the relevant branches.

## 4. Positive width: three unique active continuous directions and all-menu patterns

Fix sigma small as above and let L range over its compact displayed
interval. For a diagonal mark (s,s), let q_j(s,h,L) be the minimum own
smoothed cap mass in the closed branch where vertex j maximizes u.
At h=0 and s near 3t_sigma-1 the three unique branch minima in Section2
are proper cuts and lie in the interiors of their angular branches.

These three unique minima persist smoothly for small h, uniformly in L.
Here no nonsmooth optimization assertion is needed: on neighborhoods of
the three proper minima the triangle cap mass is a smooth function of
the normal, mark and outward displacement. The uniform-kernel integral
is its average over displacement in [0,h Gamma(u)], hence is smooth
also at h=0 from the right. The positive angular second derivative gives
the local implicit-function theorem. The strict compact gap outside
these neighborhoods excludes all additional branch minima.

Coordinate-exchange symmetry gives q_B=q_C at a diagonal mark. At h=0,

    d/ds [q_A+v-q_B]=V(24t_sigma-4)/3>0.

The implicit-function theorem therefore gives a unique nearby
s=s(h,L) satisfying

    q_A(s,h,L)+v=q_B(s,h,L)=q_C(s,h,L)=Q_T(h,L).      (6)

The three actual continuous normals still span R^2 and positively
balance. The strict outside-realization margins of Section3 persist,
so each branch minimum is an ACTUAL ambient cap attaining (6).

Conversely every continuous direction belongs to a maximum-vertex
branch. In the A branch (5) bounds its mass below by q_A+v; in the B,C
branches nonnegative outside mass bounds it below by q_B or q_C.
Consequently (6) is the minimum over ALL nonvertical ambient normals
and ALL base tilts. Equality forces the direction to be the unique own
minimum of its branch, and forces precisely these outside patterns:

    A: D fully captured; R,E_L missed;
    B,C: D,R,E_L all missed.                         (7)

Every active cap at this source has ZERO outside transition coarea.
Pure-base closed caps at base0 contain T and at least one endpoint side,
so their masses exceed Q_T and are inactive.

Finally Y_T=(0,s(h,L),s(h,L)) uniquely maximizes depth on fiber0. Freeze
the three actual caps in (6). Their continuous normals positively
balance and span R^2, so every nonzero displacement of the mark has
strictly positive inner product with at least one of them. Increasing
that threshold strictly loses mass, initially by its proper own strip
and thereafter by monotonicity. Hence every other mark has smaller
depth. This certifies maximality without restricting candidate marks.

## 5. The square source, again with ALL normal directions checked

Let c=((b-1)/2,(b-1)/2)=(-2sigma,-2sigma), the center of R. For every
continuous u and every real a, a cap through (1,c) captures outside
mass at least L^2.

If E_L is not fully captured, some X_E in E_L has

    a+u.(X_E-c)<0.

On T, at relative base -1, the margin is therefore

    -a+u.(X-c)>u.(X+X_E-2c).

The point v_E=2c-X_E has both coordinates in
[4sigma,4sigma+L] subset [0,0.041]. Therefore
v_E+[-1/4,1/4]^2 is contained in T. At least half this square, of area
1/8, has positive margin. Since L^2<=16sigma<1/8, failure to capture
all of E_L costs strictly more than L^2 from T alone. Thus

    outside mass>=L^2;
    equality forces E_L full and T,D empty.          (8)

A sufficiently large positive base tilt realizes equality for EVERY
continuous direction. Let q_R(h,L) be the ordinary own smoothed maximum
depth of R with the SAME actual global width norm Gamma. Its unique
maximizer is c. Central symmetry and convex depth superlevels make c a
maximizer. Uniqueness follows from the positive own coarea/full-normal
identity, or from the already proved pure-width uniqueness argument:
two maximizing marks would share an active cap at their midpoint, and
the identical positive-section moment equation forces identical marks.

It follows that the actual depth at (1,c) is

    Q_R(h,L)=q_R(h,L)+L^2,                           (9)

and that this is its unique own-fiber maximum. Indeed a large positive
tilt gives the upper bound own-depth+L^2 at EVERY mark, while (8) proves
equality at c. Every actual active cap at (1,c) has exactly pattern (8),
and hence zero outside coarea. Pure-base caps are strictly more costly.

## 6. Tie the TWO actual sources and occupy both parities

At h=0, q_R=|R|/2=(2-4sigma)^2/2. Equations (3)--(4) give

    8sigma-8sigma^2
      <= Q_0-|R|/2 <=8sigma-(7/2)sigma^2.            (10)

This lies strictly between (2sqrt(sigma))^2 and
(4sqrt(sigma))^2. At h=0 the continuous function Q_R-Q_T thus has
opposite signs at those two L endpoints. Own cap integrals, their compact
normal minima, Sigma, and the implicit source construction above depend
continuously on (h,L). The signs persist for every sufficiently small
h>0. The intermediate value theorem supplies L=L_h in the displayed
interval such that

    Q_R(h,L_h)=Q_T(h,L_h).                           (11)

This is an exact parameter specification, not numerical fitting. All
previous all-normal and saturation statements were uniform over this
compact interval, so they apply to the body selected by (11).

At the two exposed endpoint bases, a sufficiently exposing pure-base
cap isolates their whole fibers, giving depth at most max(v,L_h^2),
strictly below the common value near2. The complete deepest base set is
therefore exactly I={0,1}, with the unique marks already identified.
Both parities of P are occupied. All active caps at BOTH deepest sources
have zero outside coarea.

The fixed parity forest sends -1 to (-1+1)/2=0, so the left fiber D is
assigned to terminal source0. It sends2 to (2+0)/2=1. There is no menu
choice hidden in these assignments.

## 7. The best captured whole-fiber response weight is BELOW Gamma_2

At zero width all coarea of the three source0 caps is on T. The usual
own-section-centroid balance gives the response probabilities

    theta_A=(4t_sigma-1)/(6t_sigma-1),
    theta_B=theta_C=t_sigma/(6t_sigma-1).             (12)

For a direct derivation use barycentrics y=(1-2t,t,t),
r_i=1-2y_i, q_i=4 product_(j!=i)y_j. The response probability is
(r_i/q_i)/sum_j(r_j/q_j), which yields (12). In particular

    0<theta_A<1/3<4/9.                              (13)

At positive width all active source0 caps have one of the SAME THREE
unique continuous directions from Section4; their possible base tilts
do not change their outside patterns or their own coareas. The positive
balance of these three spanning directions is unique up to scale.
Dividing its raw coefficients by the respective positive coareas and
renormalizing therefore fixes unique TOTAL response weights
omega_A(h,L),omega_B(h,L),omega_C(h,L), for EVERY balanced active menu,
including menus with repeated directions and different base tilts.

These weights converge uniformly in L to (12). Reducing h if necessary,

    omega_A(h,L_h)<3/8<Gamma_2.                      (14)

By (7), A caps are exactly the active caps that capture the whole D.
Thus (14) is the captured response weight of D for EVERY balanced active
menu at its forest terminal source0. Taking the best menu cannot improve
it. This disproves the proposed pointwise Gamma whole-fiber-weight
upgrade from full source parity, zero outside coarea, and the positive
support-width reserve. It does not disprove a global allocation inequality.

## 8. The full convex-field capacity still pays on an isolated own facet

The own facet F of T opposite A is x+y=1, with outer normal (1,1).
The squares R,E_L have no positive-length facets in that normal. D's
parallel facet lies on x+y=-2+3sigma. A nonnegative continuous normal
bump supported near (1,1), zero on all the other finitely many fiber
facet normals, times the convex physical function

    Phi(z,x,y)=[x+y+2-3sigma]_+

therefore isolates the ENTIRE facet F: it is the constant3-3sigma
there, and zero on D's parallel facet. No positive-area source or
outside facet with another normal is charged. Vertices have zero
ordinary facet area.

At h=0 the weighted captured fraction of F is exactly

    4t_sigma^2/(6t_sigma-1)
      =4/9+4(3t_sigma-1)^2/[9(6t_sigma-1)]>4/9.      (15)

This is the already proved simplex own-section affine-neutral facet
identity, applied with the actual weights (12), not a new arbitrary
centroid choice. Directly, the A cap has zero trace on F, while the
B,C cap trace fractions and their weights give (15).

For fixed sigma>0 the margin in (15) is positive, although of order
sigma^4. Actual kernel traces, normals and response weights converge
on F, and all other charged facet traces remain absent. Hence for all
sufficiently small h>0 the SAME physical field has capture efficiency
strictly greater than Gamma_2. The width must be small relative to this
fixed margin; no uniform-in-sigma threshold is claimed.

The counterexample thus separates whole-assigned-fiber response weight
from the full convex-field capacity. It confirms precisely why the
additional all-facet contact geometry in a thin-edge vacancy argument
cannot be replaced by the forest support reserve alone.

# Full source parity does not give Gamma whole-fiber response weight, even for the best menu

**Full occupied parity does not force assigned whole-fiber Gamma weight**

In the source's positive-width pure outward-smoothed model there is an actual lattice-compatible four-base triangle/square family, with bases -1,0,1,2 and a parameter choice giving exactly two deepest sources in the two parity classes. For every balanced active menu of the triangle source, the response weight on the sole direction that captures its assigned endpoint fiber is less than 3/8<4/9=gamma_2. Thus full occupied source parity does not force the proposed gamma_2 assigned-whole-fiber response payment, even after optimizing the menu. This is a failure of that auxiliary allocation rule, not of total convex-field capacity or ordinary OC.

Scope limits: The opposite isolatable source facet still has efficiency 4t^2/(6t-1)>4/9. Total convex-field capacity and OC are not refuted.
